academic_translation:
If by means of a single suffering
Many sufferings are eliminated,
By the compassionate one, that suffering
Should certainly be generated for oneself and others.
translation: If facing one single suffering removes many other sufferings, a kind person should certainly take on that suffering for themselves and others.

academic_translation:
When sentient beings are liberated,
The ocean of joy that exists—
Is that itself not sufficient?
What is the use of desiring liberation?
translation: When living beings are freed, there is an ocean of joy. Is that joy not enough? What is the use of wanting freedom?

academic_translation:
Through habituation, regarding others'
Drops of semen and blood,
Even though there is an absence of an entity,
Just as one knows them as "I",
translation: By getting used to it, I take the drops of seed and blood from others as "I". Even though they are without a thing, I still call them "I".

academic_translation:
Through wishing for oneself to be exalted,
One will be reborn in a lower realm, base, and stupid.
If that very wish is shifted to others,
One will obtain a happy realm and respect.
translation: If I wish to be great myself, I will be reborn in an unhappy realm as someone low and foolish. If I shift that wish to others, I will gain a happy realm and respect.

academic_translation:
If one does not truly exchange
One's own happiness and the suffering of others,
Buddhahood will not be achieved,
And even in saṃsāra there is no happiness.
translation: If I do not truly exchange my own happiness for the suffering of others, I will never reach the state of a Buddha. Even in the cycle of rebirth, I will find no happiness.

academic_translation:
Completely abandoning the perfect joy
That achieves seen and unseen happiness,
Through the cause of inflicting suffering on others,
One takes on unbearable suffering through delusion.
translation: Out of confusion, I cause suffering to others. This brings me unbearable suffering, and I throw away the perfect joy that brings happiness I can see and cannot see.

academic_translation:
Having made the inferior and so forth into oneself,
And having made oneself into others,
With a mind free of conceptual thought,
Meditate on envy, rivalry, and pride.
translation: See a lower person and others as yourself. Then see yourself as them. Clear your mind of busy thinking. Practice feeling jealousy, rivalry, and pride.

academic_translation:
In short, for your own sake,
Whatever harm you have done to others,
For the sake of sentient beings,
Let that harm descend upon yourself.
translation: In short, whatever harm you have done to others for your own sake, let that same harm fall upon yourself, for the sake of all living beings.

academic_translation:
Yet, even when instructed in that way,
if you, my mind, do not act like that,
since all faults rely upon you,
there is nothing left but to subdue you yourself.
translation: Even when I tell you what to do, if you, my mind, do not act that way, I must defeat you. All faults rely on you, so I have no other choice.

academic_translation:
That former time when you ruined me
Was another time;
Now I see you—where will you go?
I shall destroy all your haughtiness.
translation: That past time when you ruined me is over. Now I see you. Where will you go? I will destroy all of your feeling superior.

academic_translation:
In that way, you have handed me over time and again,
And I have suffered for a long time;
I, remembering those grudges,
Will destroy your thinking of your own welfare.
translation: In that way, you have handed me over again and again. I have suffered for a long time. I remember those grudges. Now I will destroy your thoughts about your own good.

academic_translation:
Therefore, without attachment, I
Shall give up the body to benefit beings.
Thus, although it has many faults,
I shall retain it like an instrument for action.
translation: So, without being attached, I will give up my body to help others. It has many faults. Still, I will keep it like a tool for getting things done.

academic_translation:
Even yogis, due to differences in intellect,
are invalidated by those successively higher,
through examples accepted by both,
because, for the sake of the result, they are not analyzed.
translation: Meditation masters are not all equal in their thinking minds. A higher master proves a lower one wrong. They use examples they both agree on. They do not question these examples because they just want a result.

academic_translation:
"Since even a Buddha would cycle [in saṃsāra],
What is the use of the conduct of awakening?"
If the continuum of conditions is not severed,
Even an illusion does not cease;
translation: Someone might say, "Since even a Buddha would keep going around in the cycle of rebirth, what is the use of the way of acting for awakening?" I reply: As long as the unbroken flow of circumstances is not cut, even an illusion will not stop.

academic_translation:
"If, because one endowed with other conditions sees,
it is luminous to itself,"
through the application of accomplished eye ointment,
the vase is seen, but not the eye ointment itself.
translation: Someone might say, "Because the mind uses other circumstances to see, it shines to itself." Using magic eye ointment lets you see a vase. But it does not let you see the eye ointment itself.

academic_translation:
Since a non-entity depends on an entity,
How could it be endowed with a function?
Your mind, without a companion,
Would become entirely solitary.
translation: If a non-existent thing depends on a thing, how could it do anything? Your mind would have no companion. It would be completely alone.

academic_translation:
When one asserts, "Such and such does not exist,"
And the entity to be analyzed is not apprehended,
At that time, how can a non-entity lacking a basis
Remain before the intellect?
translation: When you say, "This does not exist," and you look closely at the thing but cannot find it, what happens? How can a non-existent thing without a base stay in front of the thinking mind?

academic_translation:
Likewise, in accordance with the conduct of awakening,
The shrine of the Victor, too, has been accomplished;
Even when the bodhisattva has passed
Into nirvāṇa, it accomplishes all aims.
translation: In the same way, following the way of acting for awakening, the shrine of the Victorious One has been built. Even after the awakening hero passes into freedom from sorrow, it still achieves every goal.

academic_translation:
"If the Mahāyāna is not established,
How is your scripture established?"
"Because this is established for both of us."
Initially, this was not established for you.
translation: Someone might ask, "If the Great Vehicle is not proven, how is your sacred text proven?" The answer is, "Because it is proven for both of us." But at first, it was not proven for you.

academic_translation:
"If you say it is because the Mahāyāna is subject to dispute,"
Regarding scripture, there is dispute with non-Buddhists,
And regarding other scriptures, with your own and other schools;
Since they are subject to dispute, they would be discarded.
translation: Someone might say, "We reject the Great Vehicle because people argue about it." But you argue with a non-Buddhist about your sacred text. You also argue about other sacred texts, both with your own groups and with other groups. Since people argue about them, you would have to throw them all away.

academic_translation:
If being a monk is the root of the teaching,
Even being a monk is difficult to establish.
For those whose minds have apprehension,
Even nirvāṇa is difficult to establish.
translation: If being a monk is the root of the teaching, even being a monk is hard to prove. For people whose minds are holding on to things, even freedom from sorrow is hard to prove.

academic_translation:
If you say it is certain that, for the time being,
The craving that is the cause of grasping does not exist,
Even if that craving is not afflicted,
Why would it not exist, just like delusion?
translation: Someone might say it is certain that, for now, the wanting that causes holding on does not exist. Even if that wanting is not troubled by troubling emotion, why would it not exist, just as confusion still exists?

academic_translation:
A mind that is devoid of emptiness,
Though ceased, will arise again,
Like the meditative absorption of non-perception;
Therefore, one should meditate on emptiness.
translation: A mind that has not understood emptiness will start up again even after it stops. It is like a deep meditation with no perceiving. Because of this, you should meditate on emptiness.

academic_translation:
If, due to a single unincluded one,
All become faulty,
Then due to a single one similar to a sūtra,
Why are they not all spoken by the Victor?
translation: You say that leaving out one text makes them all faulty. But if just one is like a teaching text, why are they not all spoken by the Victorious One?

academic_translation:
For the sake of those suffering through delusion,
Being freed from the extremes of attachment and fear,
Remaining in saṃsāra is accomplished—
This is the result of emptiness.
translation: For the sake of those who experience suffering from confusion, a person who is free from the extremes of clinging and fear can stay in the cycle of rebirth. This is the result of emptiness.
